name: Cutout Animation
visualIdentity: Photographic cutouts, paper, drawn objects, and lettering share a theme. Preserve cut edges, slight paper thickness, consistent contact shadows, clear pivots and occlusion, and limited parallax. The palette is reference-dependent; the suggested neutral paper tokens apply only to new presentation elements, never to source artwork.
suitableUses: Suitable for illustrated narratives, explainers, mascots, editorial shorts, and cultural or music promos when photos and drawn pieces share a theme. Can support video or interactive HTML; these are inferred uses, not verified source-video details.
limitations: Avoid joint gaps, intersections, conflicting shadows, exposed layer edges, reversed depth, or floating pieces without contact. Do not infer a fixed palette or stop-motion cadence from the style name. Character gaze needs suitable eye layers or a rig; omit it if it distorts anatomy or distracts. Keep transitions and story steps purposeful.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. Preserve task, brand, reference, and source-asset colors exactly. Optional tokens for new presentation elements only: background #F0E5D0, foreground #3B3C34, accent #987A5C; use discrete colors with no gradient. The accent fails the suggested normal-text contrast target against the background; place body text on an approved contrasting backing and check actual composites.
motionAndInteraction: Define pivots and occlusion; animate placing, peeling, hinged movement, pose replacement, or restrained layer parallax. Held poses or continuous keyframes are both valid; 12 fps art cadence is optional within higher-rate delivery. For interactive HTML, pointer or scroll input may drive bounded, reversible gaze, chapter handoffs, or narrative states when the scene supports them; provide neutral/static and reduced-motion states. Video uses authored seekable time, never live input.
audio: Unspecified and task-dependent. Suggest music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence to suit the subject and requirements; none is mandatory. Synchronize picture and sound, keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping, and review the mix with the delivered output.
assetRequirements: Prepare cutout masks and paper edges; organize pieces by pivot and define occlusion. Choose photo and drawn assets that share a theme. Preserve original materials and colors. Cache or deterministically generate textures and geometry. Supply separate facial layers or a suitable rig for gaze, if used. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
combinations: Works alone when source photos and drawn pieces cohere. Optional photocopy lettering can add editorial emphasis to new type only, with fixed grain and shared shadow direction; do not add its red accent. Restrained foreground, middle, and back-layer parallax can add depth if margins, contact, pivots, and occlusion remain intact. Chapter transitions or scroll storytelling suit meaningful progression, with readable endpoints and coherent reverse states.
productionApproach: Choose visual renderer and motion engine for the assets and required fidelity; PixiJS can composite 2D sprites, while GSAP can provide seekable authored motion. Python with Pillow, or Node.js with Sharp, can preprocess masks and images; Rough.js is optional for drawn contours, not authentic media or pose animation. Use one owner per animated property and deterministic state at composition time. HyperFrames is the primary assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only for a verified limitation and record why. Interactive pointer/scroll behavior is for HTML, not video. Verify representative states and seeks.
